body: Not important for a fix, but keeping this list up to date won't be convenient. This feels like something that should be part of `ClassDB` and defined in the `bind_methods` near the method definition:

I'd slap a big TODO here because these dictionaries should really be structs once implemented properly. If this list is to be inserted in **ClassDB** it should not be present in release builds as it serves no purpose.

For readability each of these "name conditions" could be its own individual line, or at least split in two?

We could also easily(?) have the same logic for just a few methods for typed dictionaries, so worth keeping that in mind for another time.

Yeah originally I only wanted to maintain as much functionality as possible, but I used those Array methods to test some assumptions, and figured I could just leave them in. Doing the same for dict would definitely make sense. Also fixing the return type of `get_script` from `Variant` to `Script` here should be possible.

As for splitting the lines, I tried but for some reason my clang format always fixes it back to one line.

Yeah this is a big hack for something that eventually should be solved by structs. I see no point in making a proper system in ClassDB out of this hack. For the few methods we have we can just add a comment at the point were they are bound similar to the "keep enums in sync" comments we have at some places.

I also see no point in making this exhaustive, we can add a handful of very common methods like `intersect_ray`. But beyond that we should just wait for a proper struct based solution.
clang-format can be particularly finicky when it comes to multilining conditionals for some reason. I really need to dig into why that is…
I for one would love to have it be exhaustive _enough_, and am up for the challenge of filling this list. Great autocompletion does wonders.
Oftentimes the additional lines of the `if` statement need to be indented twice (and I frankly hate it very much it looks terrible)
Feel free to add new entries if you have some methods that come to mind. I just don't want to do an exhaustive search for methods of this kind myself.
